scope: Escherichia coli flagellar motor model states used by UNI-FLAGELLUM

sources.role: Cryo-EM structural constraint on directional switching
Published interpretation connecting local stator torque, motor-subunit conformations, and switching

mappings.structuralMeaning: Two switch-compatible conformational families of one C-ring subunit
mappings.notClaimed: A one-to-one assignment to a uniquely resolved atomic microstate

mappings.structuralMeaning: Whether a modeled C-ring subunit is in a stator-contact sector at that instant
mappings.notClaimed: A directly imaged dynamic engagement variable

mappings.structuralMeaning: Coarse counts of plus-family engaged and unengaged subunits

mappings.notClaimed: A known stator conformation, catch-bond state, or molecular intermediate

mappings.structuralMeaning: Occupied versus unoccupied candidate stator slot on a periodic 13-site abstraction
mappings.notClaimed: A resolved 13-site E. coli stator ring

knownConflicts.issue: The finite-lattice reanalysis fixes L=13, whereas the currently ingested E. coli single-motor remodeling data use lower observed occupancies and classic measurements establish at least 11 torque-generating units rather than a universally resolved 13-slot ring.
knownConflicts.consequence: L=13 remains an assay-specific statistical lattice size and cannot be treated as CAD-ready molecular geometry.

knownConflicts.issue: The DLT hidden timescales are not molecularly identified by the dwell-time observations.
knownConflicts.consequence: A physical gear or printed state labeled as a molecular weak/strong state would exceed the evidence.

cadRule: Only dimensions and state multiplicities with direct structural provenance may drive CAD. Phenomenological states must be rendered as transparent mathematical layers, not literal molecular geometry.
